bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in JS_CallInternal OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=416298149 ``` Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: JS_CallInternal JS_EvalFunctionInternal __JS_EvalInternal ```
bug_description.normalized: The staged JavaScript input is accepted by `JS_Eval`, parsed into bytecode containing `OP_for_in_start`, and executed by `JS_CallInternal`. When that opcode runs, `js_for_in_start` forwards the stack value into `build_for_in_iterator`, which immediately treats `obj` as a valid `JSObject *` after only checking its tag. For the witnessed input, `p = JS_VALUE_GET_OBJ(obj)` yields an invalid pointer, and the subsequent read `if (p->fast_array)` dereferences memory 27 bytes before a live heap object, producing the recorded ASan heap-buffer-overflow read at `quickjs.c:15495`.

source.description: First project-code parser step that consumes the attacker-controlled JavaScript source and builds the function bytecode later executed on the crashing path.
source.value_from: The staged testcase `gt_results/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2025-346/poc` is passed by the libFuzzer harness into `JS_Eval(ctx, (const char *)null_terminated_data, size, "<none>", JS_EVAL_TYPE_GLOBAL)`. `__JS_EvalInternal` is the first project parser that materializes vulnerability-relevant execution state from those bytes.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: The code derives `p` from `obj` with `JS_VALUE_GET_OBJ(obj)` and immediately dereferences `p->fast_array` without validating that the value reaching `OP_for_in_start` still denotes a valid in-bounds object pointer.
root_cause.note: The saved ASan trace reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at `build_for_in_iterator /gt/_work/src/quickjs.c:15495:12`, which is exactly this field access.

sink.description: Crash site. Reading `p->fast_array` dereferences the invalid object pointer and performs the recorded heap out-of-bounds read.
sink.note: ASan recorded `READ of size 1` on address `0x507000000005`, 27 bytes before the allocated region `[0x507000000020,0x507000000068)`, with frame 0 at this statement.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific parser admission point. The staged JavaScript bytes are accepted by the QuickJS source parser and compiled into a function body instead of failing syntax parsing.

tainted_value_origin.code: JSValue val = JS_Eval(ctx, (const char *)null_terminated_data, size, "<none>", JS_EVAL_TYPE_GLOBAL);
tainted_value_origin.description: The libFuzzer harness passes the staged testcase bytes and their exact length into `JS_Eval` as JavaScript source.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The exact attacker-controlled bytes are the staged testcase file `gt_results/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2025-346/poc`, reproduced in Stage 01's saved run.

fine_trace.note: Source. The attacker-controlled bytes are parsed as JavaScript source and converted into QuickJS function bytecode for later execution.
When the admitted script contains a `for...in` loop, the parser emits the `OP_for_in_start` bytecode that will invoke enumeration setup on the loop operand at runtime.
The interpreter executes the emitted `OP_for_in_start` and passes the current stack operand `sp[-1]` into `js_for_in_start`, reaching the vulnerable enumeration initializer.

Root cause and sink. After `p = JS_VALUE_GET_OBJ(obj)`, the code immediately reads `p->fast_array`. For the witnessed input this pointer is invalid, so the field access performs the recorded 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read before the allocated object region.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan trace reports frame 0 at `build_for_in_iterator /gt/_work/src/quickjs.c:15495:12`, which is the exact sink step anchored at `if (p->fast_array) {`.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `build_for_in_iterator -> js_for_in_start -> JS_CallInternal -> JS_EvalFunctionInternal -> __JS_EvalInternal` matches fine-trace step 4 reached from step 3, with step 2 explaining why `OP_for_in_start` exists in the executed bytecode.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The staged PoC bytes are parsed at step 1, produce `OP_for_in_start` at step 2, cause the interpreter to call `js_for_in_start` with the loop operand at step 3, and that operand is dereferenced as `p->fast_array` at step 4.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 1` in `build_for_in_iterator /gt/_work/src/quickjs.c:15495:12` while running `fuzz_eval` on the staged `poc` file.

format.name: QuickJS JavaScript source
format.contract: The witness is a JavaScript source file accepted by `JS_Eval` and compiled into bytecode containing a `for...in` loop, such that executing the emitted `OP_for_in_start` passes a value into `build_for_in_iterator` whose `JS_VALUE_GET_OBJ(obj)` result is invalid and makes `if (p->fast_array)` read one byte out of bounds. The saved evidence proves this exact trigger for the supplied `poc` only; it does not justify a broader input family beyond that admitted script path.

evidence_limitations: The staged repository metadata names fix commit `1021e3c7297cbe1f5e5f3ebbc6ee7a25b4095d52`, but that commit's local diff only changes `js_promise_try` signatures and does not mention the crashing `for...in` path. Stage 02 therefore treats the vulnerable source and recorded ASan trace as the authoritative evidence for this sample and does not claim a source-grounded fix rationale from the provided patch artifacts.
No dynamic re-execution, patch validation, or additional runtime disambiguation was performed in Stage 02 by design.
